arxiv-2111-02858.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Carlos I. Pérez-Sánchez. We focus on functional renormalization for ensembles of several (say n ≥ 1 n\geq 1 ) random matrices, whose potentials include multi-traces, to wit, the probability measure contains factors of the form exp [ − Tr ( V 1 ) × … × Tr ( V k ) ] \exp[-\mathrm{Tr}(V_{1})\times\ldots\times\mathrm{Tr}(V_{k})] for certain noncommutative polynomials V 1 , … , V k ∈ ℂ ⟨ n ⟩ V_{1},\ldots,V_{k}\in\mathbb{C}_{\langle n\rangle} in the n n matrices.

arxiv-2305-14250.title: Language Models with Rationality
arxiv-2305-14250.creator: Nora Kassner Oyvind Tafjord Ashish Sabharwal Kyle Richardson, Hinrich Schütze Peter Clark
arxiv-2305-14250.description: Abstract While large language models (LLMs) are proficient at question-answering (QA), it is not always clear how (or even if) an answer follows from their latent “beliefs”. This lack of interpretability is a growing impediment to widespread use of LLMs.

arxiv-2307-00868.title: MADS: Modulated Auto-Decoding SIREN for time series imputation
arxiv-2307-00868.creator: Tom Bamford, Elizabeth Fons, Yousef El-laham, Svitlana Vyetrenko
arxiv-2307-00868.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tom Bamford, Elizabeth Fons, Yousef El-laham, Svitlana Vyetrenko. Time series imputation remains a significant challenge across many fields due to the potentially significant variability in the type of data being modelled. Whilst traditional imputation methods often impose strong assumptions on the underlying data generation process, limiting their applicability, researchers have recently begun to investigate the potential of deep learning for this task, inspired by the strong performance shown by these models in both classification and regression problems across a range of applications.

arxiv-2505-22059.creator: E. Kowalski, T. Untrau
arxiv-2505-22059.description: Abstract . The Wasserstein distance between probability measures on compact spaces provides a natural “invariant” quantitative measure of equidistribution, which is somewhat similar to the classical discrepancy appearing in Erdős–Turán type inequalities in the case of tori, but is a more intrinsic quantity.

arxiv-2510-23920.title: Nonparametric Identification and Estimation of Ratios of Multi-Category Means under Preferential Sampling
arxiv-2510-23920.creator: Grant Hopkins, Sarah Teichman, Ellen Graham, Amy D. Willis
arxiv-2510-23920.description: Abstract Multi-category data arise in diverse fields including marketing, chemistry, public policy, genomics, political science, and ecology. We consider the problem of estimating ratios of category-specific means in a fully nonparametric setting, allowing for both observational units and categories to be preferentially sampled. We consider covariate-adjusted and unadjusted estimands that are non-parametrically defined and straightforward to interpret.

Fascination with the concept of superconducting (SC) superfluid density ρ s \rho_{s} has persisted since the beginning of superconductivity theory, with numerical values of an actual density rarely provided. Over time ρ s \rho_{s} , addressed mostly in cuprate and following high temperature superconductors, has become synonymous with the normalized (unitless) inverse square of the magnetic penetration depth λ L \lambda_{L} (the London expression, with superfluid density denoted n s n_{s} ), with interest primarily on its temperature T T dependence

pmc-10579610.title: Quercetagetin alleviates zearalenone-induced liver injury in rabbits through Keap1/Nrf2/ARE signaling pathway
pmc-10579610.creator: Fengyang Wu, Fengxia Wang, Zhaohong Tang, Xinyu Yang, Yanhua Liu, Man Zhao, Shudong Liu, Shuaijuan Han, Zhisheng Zhang, Baojiang Chen
pmc-10579610.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Introduction: This study aimed to assess the alleviative effect of quercetagetin (QG) on zearalenone (ZEN)-induced liver injury in rabbits. Methods: Ninety 41-day-old healthy Hyla rabbits were randomly assigned into three groups, including a control (fed with basic diet), ZEN addition group (fed with basic diet + 600 μg/kg ZEN), and ZEN + QG addition group (fed with basic diet + 600 μg/kg ZEN + 100 mg/kg QG), with 30 rabbits per group. The duration of the experiment was 28 days.

pmc-10755416.title: Energy and nutrient content of school lunches provided for children attending school-based nurseries: a cross-sectional study
pmc-10755416.creator: Claire J Wall, Jo Pearce
pmc-10755416.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Objective:To nutritionally analyse lunches provided for 3–4-year-old children attending school nurseries. Energy and nutrient content are compared with nutrient frameworks underpinning voluntary guidelines for early years settings (EYS) and mandatory standards for infant schools (4–7-year-olds).Design:A cross-sectional study, recording all main meals, vegetarian meals, jacket potato options, sandwich options and all desserts and accompaniments provided over 5 consecutive days in each school. Two portions of each meal were collected each day and weighed.

pmc-11367553.description: Due to consistent cassava cultivation, small-scale processing centers rely heavily on the cassava grater. Adding to these challenges is the competitive global market, demanding a focus on design enhancements.

pmc-12615725.title: A century of change in the California Current: upwelling system amplifies acidification
pmc-12615725.creator: Mary Margaret V. Stoll, Curtis A. Deutsch, Hana Jurikova, James W. B. Rae, Hartmut Frenzel, Anne M. Gothmann, Simone R. Alin, Alexander C. Gagnon
pmc-12615725.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Predicting the pace of acidification in the California Current System (CCS), a productive upwelling system that borders the west coast of North America, is complex because the anthropogenic contribution is intertwined with other natural sources. A central question is whether acidification in the CCS will follow the pace of increasing atmospheric CO2, or if climate effects and other biogeochemical processes will either amplify or attenuate acidification.

pmc-12723459.title: Thermally Activated Stereoinversion in Benzotrithiophene‐Based Supramolecular Polymers with Water as the Effector
pmc-12723459.creator: Lucía López‐Gandul, Alberto Fernández‐Alarcón, Nicolás M. Casellas, Cristina Naranjo, Joaquín Calbo, Enrique Ortí, Miguel García‐Iglesias, Luis Sánchez
pmc-12723459.description: We report the synthesis of the chiral benzotrithiophene (BTT) derivative 1, which self‐assembles into helical supramolecular polymers. The C 3 symmetry of BTT 1 enables a unique temperature‐dependent stereomutation process in which water acts as a key effector. Circular dichroism measurements reveal that a higher water content induces a double stereomutation, ultimately restoring the original helicity.

pmc-12949857.title: Exploration of safety indicators for radiotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma: A real-world study
pmc-12949857.creator: 雪忆 谢, 曦 张, 红华 彭, 隽 张, 宇亮 潘, 震 张, 乔 金, 培国 曹
pmc-12949857.description: ObjectiveHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common pathological subtype of primary liver cancer and is associated with high incidence and mortality. External beam radiation therapy (EBRT) is a widely used local treatment modality for HCC across different disease stages. In the era of precision radiotherapy, standardized safety evaluation indicators for HCC radiotherapy remain lacking.

pmc-13064528.title: A method of estimating cervical cancers prevented by the introduction of national screening in Ireland
pmc-13064528.creator: David Robert Grimes, Aline Brennan, Cathal Walsh
pmc-13064528.description: Cervical cancer screening is a life-saving endeavour. The introduction of an organized population-based national screening programmes has potential to both reduce incidence of cervical cancer in an asymptomatic population and detect early-stage cancers for accelerated treatment. A methodology for estimating cancers prevented by such programmes has immediate utility.

pmc-13159307.title: Gender differences in a causal model of risk factors underlying early alcohol sipping
pmc-13159307.creator: Andrea Maxwell, Kathryn Cullen, Erich Kummerfeld, Rajita Sinha, Anna Zilverstand
pmc-13159307.description: BackgroundEarly alcohol sipping with permission, here defined as tasting alcohol without necessarily taking a full drink by late childhood with parental permission, is an early marker of future problematic alcohol use. This study aimed to generate an initial data-driven causal model of the potential risk factors underlying early alcohol sipping and probe gender differences in this model.

pmc-13266814.title: Computed tomography features associated with pneumothorax susceptibility in pectus excavatum: a retrospective case-control study of lobar morphometry, attenuation metrics, and machine-learning projection
pmc-13266814.creator: In Sub Kim, Jae Jun Kim, Kyong Shil Im, Yoon Ho Kim, Jeong Hwan Ryu
pmc-13266814.description: BackgroundPrimary spontaneous pneumothorax (PSP) can occur without visible blebs or bullae, suggesting a broader structural susceptibility. Pectus excavatum (PE) is associated with a high incidence of PSP. We evaluated chest computed tomography (CT)-based lobar signatures of PSP and tested whether PE exhibits a PSP-like phenotype.

pmc-13415836.title: A Review of Transition Metal Phosphides for Hydrazine-Assisted Electrolytic Water Splitting for Hydrogen Production
pmc-13415836.creator: Minghao Yuan, Jun Wang, Xiaoqing Liao, Junhan Wang, Minghao Bian, Jingwen Ma
pmc-13415836.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Electrochemical water splitting for hydrogen production is an important path for the preparation of green hydrogen. However, the sluggish kinetics and high energy consumption of the anode oxygen evolution reaction (OER) have restricted its development. The hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR), with its low theoretical potential, fast kinetics, clean products, and the ability to simultaneously treat hydrazine-containing wastewater, has emerged as an ideal anode reaction to replace OER.
